teams.heading: Vinaya Habosi beats four defenders for Fiji try in France loss
teams.body: Centre Vinaya Habosi beat four defenders to score, one of Fiji's two tries in Saturday's 54-17 defeat in Lyon. Selestino Ravutaumada added a second consolation try, but coach Jake White's side, who started with 10 France-based players including their entire backline, slumped to a fourth straight defeat in the inaugural Nations Championship. Their backs struggled to fire, and Jiuta Wainiqolo, playing in his adopted home, was unable to make an impact.

lead.why: It is the only shortlist item about Fiji's own play; the NEW items are Ireland team news, which cannot lead.

teams.heading: Borthwick fears Feyi-Waboso and Atkinson may miss Japan test after Wallabies win
teams.body: Injury news keeps coming for England before Saturday's meeting with Japan. Immanuel Feyi-Waboso hurt an ankle in the first half against Australia, was replaced at half-time and was later seen in a moon boot, while Seb Atkinson came off with a hip problem after the break. Head coach Steve Borthwick said of Atkinson: "We're talking days to recover, maybe not available next weekend, but it's really too early for me to say that." Both men had already missed England's pre-Nations Championship alignment camp while rehabilitating.

lead.why: A new injury story with England's own head coach on record, and it bears directly on Saturday's test against Japan.

teams.heading: Dupont and Lucu struggle to link at half-back before Springboks test
teams.body: Antoine Dupont and Maxime Lucu struggled to build a rhythm at half-back in France's 54-17 win over Fiji, losing possession and rarely getting long phases together. Lucu said France lost plenty of ball in the first half, often at the third or fourth ruck, which stopped them setting up their game. He credited Dupont with well-timed switches in the smaller channels, a plan the pair had targeted before the match. Rugbyrama says the combination must be sorted before France face South Africa on Friday.

lead.why: The newest France-focused item, on the half-back pairing that must work against South Africa.

teams.heading: Nick Timoney says he is grateful for Ireland starts after long wait
teams.body: Ulster back row Nick Timoney says the long wait for Ireland chances has made him value every appearance. The 31-year-old debuted against the USA in 2021 but added only two caps in the next four years amid a crowded back row; this year he has played all nine Ireland matches across the Six Nations and Nations Championship, three as a starter. He told BBC Sport NI: "I'm grateful for it and trying not to think too big picture about it."

lead.why: It is the strongest new Ireland item on the shortlist, with corroboration across two outlets, and it is not the Sheehan injury already reported today.

teams.heading: Danilo Fischetti says Italy want to show character after Springboks loss
teams.body: Danilo Fischetti, the Northampton Saints prop who came off the bench in Turin, admits the Springboks game was gone before he arrived. Italy had prepared well during the week, he said, but failed to carry that into the match, leaving the squad frustrated and disappointed. Looking ahead to Saturday's test in Genoa, Fischetti said Italy want to show their character, with the front row decisive against an Argentina side under pressure at set-piece but with plenty of potential.

lead.why: A fresh on-record reaction from an Italy player ahead of the Argentina test, and the only new Italy item on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Scotland Supporters Club deadline 23 November for Six Nations pre-sale access
teams.body: Fans who want priority access to tickets for Scotland's three home fixtures at the 2027 Guinness Men's Six Nations must buy a Scotland Supporters Club membership by midnight on Monday 23 November. The pre-sale opens on Tuesday 24 November, with any remaining tickets going on general sale on Thursday 26 November. SSC Matchday costs £50 a year and includes pre-sale access to Scotland Men's home internationals and both legs of the 1872 Cup. Memberships run January to December, so fans buying now must redeem them come the new year.

teams.heading: Louis Rees-Zammit urges Wales to be brave against All Blacks in Cardiff
teams.body: Louis Rees-Zammit, named player of the match against Japan, says Wales must attack the All Blacks rather than shy away from them. He gained 110 metres from 11 runs against Japan, with three clean breaks and 14 defenders beaten. Recalling last year's 52-26 defeat in Cardiff, when Wales were competitive until around the hour mark, he said the team must "be fearless" with the ball. "Next week will be brave and go for it," he added, warning that stepping back invites punishment from the All Blacks.

lead.why: Fresh player comment on Saturday's All Blacks test, and the newest Wales item not already run.

teams.heading: Italy prop Danilo Fischetti vows reaction against Argentina after South Africa defeat
teams.body: Italy begin preparations with a prop's warning: Danilo Fischetti said the Azzurri want a response on Saturday, not just a result. Speaking at the press conference after the squad's first day on the grass, he said the group had already dissected the South Africa match together and wants a different performance. He also acknowledged important absences, but said they open chances for others. Argentina should expect an Italy side keen to show their character in Genoa.

teams.heading: Isaac Henry ruled out of remaining November Tests with hamstring strain
teams.body: The Wallabies confirmed on Tuesday that Isaac Henry will miss the rest of November Tests, having come off in the 58th minute at Twickenham with a hamstring strain. No replacement will join the squad, with the coaching group backing the options it has. Kiss could turn to Filipo Daugunu, who replaced Henry against England, with Kurtley Beale the other centre cover. It makes a sixth different midfield partnership in seven Tests, with Len Ikitau and Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii tipped as the likeliest pairing to face Scotland at Murrayfield.

lead.why: A fresh official Wallabies injury announcement that reshapes the midfield before the Scotland Test, unlike the opinion and post-match pieces already covered.

teams.heading: Borthwick fears Feyi-Waboso and Atkinson may miss Japan Test with injuries
teams.body: England go into their meeting with Japan with two injury doubts. Exeter Chiefs back Immanuel Feyi-Waboso picked up an ankle injury before half-time in the 45-22 win over Australia and was later seen in a moon boot, while Gloucester centre Seb Atkinson came off with a hip problem. Head coach Steve Borthwick said of Atkinson: "maybe not available next weekend". Both missed England's pre-Nations Championship camp for rehabilitation.

lead.why: It is the only genuinely new item in the shortlist; the Japan items all retell the Wales match already covered.

teams.heading: Steve Hansen says Dave Rennie has made All Blacks a different team
teams.body: Speaking to Rugby Unity after Saturday's 43-21 win at Murrayfield, Steve Hansen credited Dave Rennie's environment for an All Blacks side that is, in his words, "a different team". He pointed to props scoring from quick taps and said "There's no passengers. There's no social loafing." Hansen also acknowledged the difficult week the squad had in Scotland, following the death at the team hotel of long-serving head of security Logan Cadwallader.

lead.why: It is the freshest New Zealand item in the pack, and it is a direct verdict on the squad after Saturday's win.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus rejects favourites tag while listing Springbok absentees before France test
teams.body: Ahead of Friday's test in France, Erasmus named South Africa's absentees and argued that France's injuries do not make them clear favourites. Frans Malherbe, RG Snyman, Eben Etzebeth, Kwagga Smith, André Esterhuizen, Handré Pollard and Cheslin Kolbe are all unavailable. "So, who’s understrength?" Erasmus asked, noting France are without Romain Ntamack, Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos, while his side have a maximum of three games left in a long season.

lead.why: Fresh press-conference quotes from Rassie Erasmus on absentees and the favourites tag; the Louw selection is already reported.
